experiment: On-device clock64() scrub-region bracketing (RP Sec VI.D)
caveat: clock64() counts SM clock cycles exactly (jitter-free); ns conversion uses cudaDeviceProp.clockRate queried once at idle before the runs, so absolute ns figures inherit whatever imprecision GPU Boost/dynamic clocking introduces relative to that fixed reference. Cycle counts themselves are exact.
method: single-block kernel; __syncthreads() -> t0=clock64() -> [scrub loop + __threadfence_block() + __syncthreads()] -> t1=clock64(); thread 0 only; cycles = t1-t0; median/stddev over reps (post-warmup)

full_sm_amplification.description: RP Sec VI.D item (b): scrubs a near-max shared-memory footprint (24000 words, 93.75 KB of ~100 KB/SM ceiling) with a full-size 1024-thread block, dividing total scrub time by word count for a bandwidth-representative figure independent of any one kernel's thread geometry.

result: Fills RP Table IV's clock64() column and Sec VI.D's [[MEASURE: cycles/exit per class]] / [[MEASURE: ns/exit]] placeholders with genuinely resolved, jitter-free on-device measurements, and the amplification method's [[MEASURE: ns per word, 95% CI]] placeholder -- distinct from and more precise than benchmark.json's host-side CUDA-event upper bounds, which the scrub cost was too small to resolve against.
